task_0_spine_structure.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION -- new this round, not in the prior report
task_0_spine_structure.statement: the four R1 events are NOT independent siblings from the root. Reading literal_macro_trace together shows they are four alternative 'fire R1 now vs continue preparation' choices at increasing depth along one shared Z2-preparation spine: macro_index1 Z2 33/0->120/2(hex64), macro_index2 Z2 64/0->120/3(hex90), macro_index3 Z2 90/0->120/4(hex96), macro_index4 Z2 96/0->120/0(hex0). Event 1 fires R1 at depth 0 of this spine, event 2 at depth 1, event 3 at depth 2 (where R1 itself lands on hex0, the hub -> CH1), event 4 at depth 4 (after the spine's own Z2 already touched the hub one step earlier -> PRE_R_COMPLETER_EVENT_ORDER).
task_0_spine_structure.hub_phase_coincidence: orbit 120's phase-0 slot is identically hexagon 0 (the hub), a fixed structural fact confirmed by both event 3's R edge and event 4's spine Z2 edge landing there identically -- not a coincidence of which move type fires.

task_3_required_merging_event.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION + CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF
task_3_required_merging_event.statement: a Z2 or Z3 edge, fired while the walk is standing in (or opening) an orbit already in the R2-source-orbit's small component, whose target hexagon is already registered as part of R1-target's larger component (or the symmetric assignment) -- either merges the same two components

hand_proof_cannot_be_R.claim: the merging event cannot be an R edge, and specifically cannot be R2 itself
hand_proof_cannot_be_R.proof: this repository's own already-proven fact (r_count_exceeded, restated in RR_TARGET_A_PRUNE_SCOPE_AUDIT_CODEX.md's formal hierarchy) is that an RR word from a bare short root has exactly two R events: R1 (already fixed) and R2 (the boundary candidate itself, whose legality is exactly what is being tested, evaluated at the PRE-R2 state before it fires). A third R is provably excluded (rr_R_budget). The merging event, if one exists, must fire strictly between the fixed R1 and the not-yet-fired R2 attempt, and cannot itself be an R -- leaving only Z2 or Z3.

violates_hub_touch.answer: conditionally possible, not proven either way
violates_hub_touch.mechanism: hub_touch_count is a retained Q1-safe prune (more than two hub targets under F<=1 is illegal); depends on the specific merging edge chosen, which this data does not enumerate

destroys_terminal_geometry.answer: conditionally possible for F, not at risk for H
destroys_terminal_geometry.mechanism: F only increases on an abandonment (dF=1 when the next literal rotation of the old pass would have been unvisited); inserting any edge changes the walk's trajectory and could trigger an unwanted abandonment, pushing F from 1 to 2 (F_exceeded, monotone, retained, disqualifying). H cannot be pushed positive by any weight<=3 RR-alphabet edge (dH=max(weight-3,0)=0), so H is not at risk from this class of insertion.

changes_candidate_r2_source_orbit.reason: inserting any additional macro edge anywhere in the walk's history shifts every subsequent position, since rotation runs land differently once the preceding history has one more edge in it. The 5419 recorded candidates are candidates of the walk exactly as it stands; repairing the mismatch does not patch those specific states -- it produces a materially different walk with its own, currently unknown, R2 candidate set.

remains_legal_overall.answer: not proven impossible, not proven guaranteed
remains_legal_overall.reason: both named risk mechanisms (hub_touch_count, F_exceeded-via-abandonment) are real but neither is shown unavoidable for every possible choice of merging edge

No argument was found (and none fabricated) showing every possible Z2/Z3 merging choice, at every insertion point, must trigger F_exceeded or hub_touch_count_exceeded. task_6_minimal_repair_pattern.label: CLAUDE_PROPOSAL -- a description of what to look for, not a claim it exists, not searched for by this document
task_6_minimal_repair_pattern.event_type: Z2 or Z3 only (never R, proven excluded in task_3)
task_6_minimal_repair_pattern.source_target_orbit: source orbit already a member of the R2-source-orbit's eventual small component; target hexagon already a member of R1-target's component at the moment this edge fires
task_6_minimal_repair_pattern.timing_relative_to_completer: strictly after R1 (macro_index > 5 in this lineage) and strictly before the re-attempted R2 candidate; no constraint relative to the original completer (macro_index 4), which already fired before R1
task_6_minimal_repair_pattern.required_decoration: the walk's full component-forest state at the insertion point (to confirm the target hexagon is genuinely in R1-target's component, not merely a class-shape match) and F/H immediately after insertion (to rule out an accidental abandonment)
task_6_minimal_repair_pattern.expected_codex_search_predicate: do NOT extend the current 100250-node frontier (task_4 proves any insertion changes the downstream candidate set entirely). Instead: from the fixed post-R1 state at macro_index 5 (or any other post-R1 state), enumerate Z2/Z3 continuations and, for each, check (a) whether it merges the R2-source-orbit's component with R1-target's component, (b) whether F stays <=1 immediately after, and (c) whether hub_touch_count stays <=2 immediately after -- reporting the first (or all, if cheap) edges satisfying all three, rather than only aggregate counts
